A1.justification: Both PDFs describe successive versions of the same work, sharing the core decoder design and nuScenes experiments despite the HSTrack-to-SynCL renaming. All nine pages of each are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original HSTrack tracking/detection results and component, label-assignment and training-length ablations on nuScenes in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original SynCL results, ablations, attention analyses, filtering comparisons and training-resource measurements.

M1.justification: The shared decoder and hybrid assignment survive renaming. However, v2 introduces a two-component GMM that dynamically determines the filtering threshold, extending v1's threshold-and-bottom-k selection. The stated association objective also changes: v2 Eq. 11 excludes the positive pair from its contrastive denominator, whereas v1 uses softmax cross-entropy. These are substantive procedural and objective revisions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate multi-camera 3D tracking and detection on nuScenes, retaining the same object categories and driving domain. No additional dataset, task or distinct input-environment scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator membership, with TBQP-Baseline renamed TBA-Baseline. v2 Table 3 adds ATSS, SimOTA and DETA as evaluated alternatives for one-to-many assignment/filtering. This is a focused expansion of component-level comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds an inference-time self-attention-removal control, a maximum-assignment sweep over K = 4, 5, 6, and training-time/memory measurements. Some ablation metric sets now include NDS/mAP. The stated dataset splits, image resolutions, optimizer settings and default three-frame clips remain; the renamed frame-length sweep still tests two, three and four frames.

E4.justification: v2 adds attention-removal examples and layer heatmaps (Figures 2–3), filtering comparisons and examples (Table 3, Figure 6), matching-cap sensitivity (Table 5), and resource analysis (Figure 5). Existing component, assignment and frame-length studies remain, with v1 Table 4 corresponding to v2 Table 6. These additions substantially broaden the method's diagnostic evaluation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or result variability. The new GMM estimates matching costs within the algorithm; it is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises results across all four tracker settings: proposed-method AMOTA changes from 43.1% to 44.7% with PF-Track-S and from 46.4% to 48.5% with PF-Track-F†. PETRv2 baseline AMOTA also changes from 44.2% to 43.2%, so its larger improvement margin cannot be attributed solely to the proposed method. Ablation values change, and filtering/resource results are added.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a two-component Gaussian model for matching costs (Eq. 10) and kernel definitions with a linear-mapping derivation for association (Eqs. 12–14). These extend v1's direct cost/affinity formulation, while much decoder and matching mathematics is restated. Neither version supplies theorems or tracking guarantees.

C1.justification: v2 makes dynamic filtering and the over-deduplication/self-centric attention diagnosis central contributions, and explicitly claims new state-of-the-art tracking performance. v1 primarily claims improvements to existing trackers through hybrid and associative supervision. v2 also replaces the erroneous headline mAP improvement with an NDS improvement consistent with Table 1.

C2.justification: The central mechanism explanation expands to self-centric track attention and impaired transfer from detection pretraining. For matching all ground truths, v1 invokes interference from newborn targets; v2 instead invokes a reduced proportion of positive contrastive pairs. v2 adds filtering-selectivity and matching-cap interpretations and drops v1's general explanation that one-to-many supervision reduces false positives.

D1.justification: v2 specifies GMM components and threshold construction, the default matching cap K = 5, training-resource measurements, and a planned code/raw-results release. It omits v1's 24-epoch detector-pretraining disclosure and explicit aggregate/auxiliary-loss and weight details. These omissions do not establish that the underlying pretraining or weighting settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the dedicated hybrid-supervision survey with a stronger focus on multi-task optimization in MOT, adding positioning against OneTrack and discussion of MOTRv2/MOTRv3. It adds kernel-contrastive and adaptive-assignment references while removing substantial CNN, BEV and hybrid-supervision background. This substantively revises research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, with an explicit contribution list and an analysis section added. Method and loss exposition is reorganized. HSTrack, TBQP and U-decoder become SynCL, TBA and C-decoder, respectively; title, author/affiliation text and section numbering also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the paradigm and architecture diagrams, with v1 Figure 2 corresponding to v2 Figure 4. It adds attention visualizations, resource bars, filtering examples and two tables. Retained ablation tables change column structure and placement. These are substantial visual and layout revisions beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports its mechanism and filtering choice through attention analyses, selector comparisons and matching-cap sensitivity tests, while quantifying training overhead. Its abstract also resolves v1's mAP/NDS mismatch with Table 1. These changes improve assessability, but removing pretraining and complete loss/weight details weakens reproducibility, limiting the net quality gain.
